The time window function   of the Parzen window is narrower than the raised
cosine window.   The main lobe of the Parzen window is about 30% wider in
frequency than that of the raised- cosine (and the Hamming) window.      The
magnitude of the side lobe levels    are approximately   the same.  The side-
lobes of the Parzen window always remain positive      while those for the
raised- cosine oscilate  betwen positive  and negative values.

as if it were two cosines (at 60, 68) each of half amplitude.     These
combine to give an smplitud- modulated waveform.   The high frequency is
at the average (64) and the low frequency is at half the difference     (4) .
(Generation of a 'clean ' cosine waveform requires a submultiple of 64. )
Amplitude modulation  is covered in Chapter  5.

7.4.3         A possible receiving system for pulse timing systems in which it is knowit that there is
              zero average value in the modulating signal is proposed as follows. Timing points are
              determined and very narrow positive pulses are generated at the half-period (T/ 2)
              points. The trailing edges of the incoming pulse timing waveform arc detected and
              these generate narrow negative pulses. The resulting pulse train is applied to a constant-
              amplitude pulse generator with the following logic operation. If the first pulse to arrive
              at the generator within a clock period is positive, then a positive level is generated until
              a negative pulse arrives to terminate it. If the first pulse to arrive at the generator
              within a clock 먀riod is negative, then a negative level is generated until a positive
              pulse a口ives to terminate it. The resulting waveforms arc then smoothed with a low-
              pass filter.
              a) Will this system work satisfactorily for PPM? Explain.
              b) Will this system work satisfactorily for PWM? Explain.

        a) Yes, but only if the (modulated) trailing edges do not cross
the T/2 timing point. (If they were allowed to cross that point then the
ouput becomes multivalued and severe distortion results. ) The system
generates a PWM waveform (either in phase if the modulated timing point
follows the T/2 point, or inverted if the modulated timing point precedes
the T/2 point) , which can then be demodulated using a LPF (Prob. 7. 4.1) .
b) Yes, if the PWM waveform leading (unmodulated) timing edges are synchro-
 nized with the T/2 points. However, there is no advantage in doing this
 because it simply regenerates the PWM waveform.

        frequency modulation (FM) method, each pulse in the high state exists for onc-fourth "
        the clock interval. A one is represented by two cycles of an alternating high/low state
        pattern. A zero is represented by a high state for one-fourth the clock interval and a
        low state for three-fourths of the clock interval. In the second method, called m어ified
        frequency modulation (MFM), the high-state pulses are one-half the clock interval and
        the following encoding rule is used. A one is represented by a low State followed by a

        l們V state. It no high state occurred at the end of the previous clock interval, or by two
        consecutive low states if a high state occurred at the end of the previous clock interval.

7.8.2    a) Is it possible to make an undetected digit interchange error in Drill Problem 7.8.2?
            Expla沇
         b) Would the rule of tripling alternate digits work as well in this scheme? Explain.

          a) If one used a conventional number system, the only solution
 to the equation: 2n1+ n2 - n1+ 2n2 would be: n5 - n2. However, some
 extraneous solutions become a possibility as a result of the use of the
 modulo arithmetic. The troublesome digits in this check system are 0 's
 because they do not generate any weight other than zero, regardless of
 position in the codeword, and 9 's because the sum of the digits in any
 multiple of 9 is always nine. Thus this system allows an interchange of
 0, 9 to go undetected. In all other cases a single digit interchange is
 detectable, if no other error occurs in the codeword. With rio digit
 interchange errors present, the system acts like a parity check.
b) No, this system has the same problem with the undetectability of the
 0, 9 interchange, but it picks up another one (3, 7) . [Note: It is help-
  ful in this problem to organize a computer solution; such an approach is
  included on the diskette to accompany this solution manual. ]

7.12.4 It is suggested that a way to perform thc co口elation of two scqucnccs of pulses with
       土 I amplitudes is to rcplace each pulse with an impulse function with area 士 I, and
       perform the correlation at the various shifts to obtain the weights of a new sequence of
       impulse functions, It is argued that the autocorrclation function is the correlation of this
       new sequence of impulse functions with the autocorrelation of one pair of pulse wave-
       forms, normalized to a peak of one. Will this work? Explain. (It m ay be helpful here to

        systems. For example, the mean is a measure of the 50% p이nt in the cumulative distri-
        bution function, and the standard deviation is a measure of 小e effective width of a pdf.
        Show that, by a proper analogy, the delay time t0 and the rise time t, of a linear time
        invariant systemn with impusle response hO) can be written as [ cf. Eq. (3.80)]:

        Explain this analogy to the pdf, and to the cumulative distribution function.


        Because a probability density function (pdf) must be nonnegative
and have unit area, we represent the analogous measure in linear time-
invariant (LTI) systems as:

                                                                                        5 Ih(t) I2dt
                                                                                        戶m
                                                             time it takes the
The delay time of is LTI system is usually defined as the
system output to: attain the 50% level in the unit step response. Using
                                                            distribution
the analogy of the unit step response to the cumulative
function, this criterion corresponds to the median of the impulse
                                                                          use
response. However, the mean value (first moment) is often easier to
mathematica  lly, arid gives results approximatel y equal to the  median value
                                                               mean value,
in many cases. So we approximate the time delay t。as the
with q(t) taking the place of the pdf, in this analogy.

    The rise time of a LTI system is defined as the time difference between
 those times at which the unit step response attains two preset levels
                                                                    the
 (usually, the 10% and 90% levels) . This, in turn, is a measure of
254       제 8 장 확률과 랜덤변수
effective width of the impulse response of the system (specifically, the
10% and 90% areas) . Because the second moment is often easier to handle
mathematically, the standard deviation is used as a measure of the width
of the impulse response. So we approximate the rise time tr as the
standard deviation, with q(t) taking the place of the pdf, in this
analogy. Both of these approximations are used widely in analytical work.

8.12.1 Sunspot activity varies over time intervals of several hou八 to years. and affects high-
       frequency (HF) communications using skywave propagation in the ionosphere. Major
       sunsp아 activity is cyclic, with a full cycle on the order of 11. 1 %ears. Magnetic storms
       associated with solar activity arc cyclic in 27 day cycles, the rotation period of the sun.
       Would you classify these effects of solar activity on ionospheric propagation as station-
       ary random processes over a) a minute; b) a week? Explain.

a) Because the statistical behavior changes rapidly with respect
 to the observation interval this process cannot be considered stationary.
b) Because the statistics vary slowly with respect to the observation
 interval, this process can be considered stationary over relatively short
 time intervals. Note: Such processes are called "quasi- stationary. "
 Because many physical processes are quasi- stationary, it is important that
 one choose the observation interval carefully.

9.1.8   (Huffman Coding) It is advantageous to make the average number of digits in a code as
        nearly equal as possible to the source entropy. This can be done by assigning shorter
        codewords to more probable messages. but at the expense of variable-length code-
        words. An algorithm for generating such a code is outlined, and consists of three
        steps. The first step is to list the messages in a column in descending order of their
        probabilities of occurrence. Next, combine the last two (i.e.. those two with thc lowest
        probabilities) and list again in a second column in descending order of probabilities.
        Continue this procedure until there arc only two left in the list.
           In the second step, list the final two in the first step in a row, then place each pair
        beneath its reduction, row-by-row, retracing the steps above. In the third step, assign a
        0 and I to the top pair in the list in step two (it makes no difference if 0 or I), then
        assign a 0 or I as the second digit for entries in the second row, and continue row-by-
        row. This procedure systematically assigns shortest codewords to messages with
        highest probabilities of occurrence. Using this procedure, generate the codewords:
        a) in l)rill Problem 9. 1.2:

10.11.1 Explain why there is a significant degradation in performance in an APK system when
        the modulated signal is passed through a nonlinear (saturation-type) amplifier. Con
        sider both the case of a band-limited APK signal and one that is not band-limited.
a) For amplitude saturation but no band limiting, those signal
 states fartherest from the origin (see, e.g. , Fig. 10.42) are compressed
 toward the origin. The net result is that the distances between signal
 states for the higher 쾨nplitude levels decrease and the errors increase.
      352    제 10 장 디지탈 변조
 b) In the band-limited case, 出nplitude saturation also results in phase
  shifts.  Therefore those signal states fartherest from the origin are
  not only compressed toward the origin but their location is also rotated
  with respect to those closer to the origin. This can result in further
  decreases in distances between signal states. [Note that Q(x) is not a
  linear function, and the error effects of coining closer to one state but
  farther from another through rotation may not balance. )
